terms.gloss: hatred, hate; odium in + acc., hatred of, toward
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.21: odium (est) īra inveterāta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero calls it anger grown old. Toward someone: odium in aliquem; “be hated”, odiō esse + dat.

evidence: Plaut. Ps. 1.1.28: odiōsus mihi es (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The o is short, as in odium (Lewis & Short); Traupman marks it long.

sources: Lewis & Short: odium
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 326.
